verdict.rationale: Vendor docs describe a CLI sandbox that blocks sensitive files like ~/.ssh and .env and hides anything not explicitly mounted. They also describe Git-worktree isolation and Deny/Ask/Allow permission lists. Independent reports concretely contradict this: an indirect prompt-injection attack got the agent past its own default setting to read .env and exfiltrate the data, the default network allowlist included webhook.site as an exfiltration vector, and in one incident an agent auto-executed a command that wiped a whole drive. Missing for 10: documented network-egress sandboxing, sandbox coverage for the IDE/desktop agent (not just the CLI), in-depth sandbox docs, and independent confirmation that isolation holds against prompt injection.
